newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe's Trans Zambezi looks to expand in Africa.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe's Trans Zambezi looks to expand in Africa.

text.p: Trans Zambezi Industries Ltd, the Zimbabwe conglomerate which announced plans to list in Harare earlier this month, is looking to expand its interests into English-speaking Africa as economic reforms take root.

"We are looking further north of here and on a case by case basis we are reviewing opportunities in Anglophone countries because they have a rule of law which we can understand," chief executive officer Hillary Duckworth said on Monday.

"But we don't have any specific plans yet...we have connections in Kenya and Tanzania and Uganda has implemented very progressive investment regime which is welcoming to foreign capital," he told Reuters.
Duckworth said the success of the Zimbabwean-based conglomerate in southern Africa in the past three years had given it confidence in the region's future as a destination for investment.
"Trans Zambezi (TZI) has moved from a (U.S.) $3 million company to a $150 million company over the past three years," he said.
It has also posted over 20 percent growth in earnings per share in U.S. dollar terms since it started operating in Zimbabwe.
"From an investment point of view that's attractive. That makes people sit up and take notice. If you want to take attention of investors you have to show high returns," Duckworth said.

"This region has been unfairly regarded as high risk but if you produce high returns you attract money and we have proven it," he said, echoing a statement in the conglomerate's results for the year ended September 30 in which it asserted its intention to be a showcase to prove the case for investment in the region.
With 95 percent of its investments concentrated in Zimbabwe and Zambia, Duckworth said TZI was seeking listings on the two countries' exchanges to add to its transparency and identity in the region.
TZI has 46.3 million shares listed in Luxembourg and it plans to localise about seven percent of those shares in Zimbabwe by March this year.
With an initial market capitalisation of about Z$1.8 billion, the conglomerate will rank seventh on the Zimbabwean Stock Exchange.
"Our intention is to localise something like 20 percent of our shares over the next year in Zimbabwe," Duckworth said.
TZI has financial, food and distribution and industrial operations in Botswana, Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe. It also holds a 49 percent stake in Zimbabwe's private airline, Zimbabwe Express Airlines.
